subject: Pystan for revenue prediction (large Pareto k estimates)

messages.author: ec64b10e28226ce1
messages.subject: Pystan for revenue prediction (large Pareto k estimates)
parts:
Hi Stan experts, 

I'm using pystan to build a regression model for revenue prediction. I understand that large percentages of Pareto k estimates greater than 1 is an indication that there is something wrong with the model. There is probably influential data points in the model. Are there some sensible way to control for these caveats? Or, does that imply there is something fundamentally wrong with the model specification?

(right now it's just a multiple regression with revenue as the outcome, and 4 predictors. There are 2 layers of the model and the model is predicting 32 regions simultaneously).

Thank you in advance!
Maggie

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Pystan for revenue prediction (large Pareto k estimates)
parts:
Hi, so high values of k indicate the loo estimate can be unstable.  One alternative is to use 5-fold or 10-fold cross-validation.  This is less automatic than loo but is more stable in that you’re just re-fitting the model each time.  (It in general would be too expensive to re-fit the model for each data point, but it’s not such a big deal to re-fit 5 or 10 times to do the x-val._
A

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Pystan for revenue prediction (large Pareto k estimates)
parts:
RIght, high values of k don’t indicate problem with the model.  They indicate problem with the importance-sampling calculation of loo.

Finally, the way you penalized overprediction in Stan is to give parameters informative priors so you’re not overfitting the data.  Cross-validation can be used to compare different fitted models.

A

Thank you again in advance!
